items.title: UWM rolls out 40 bps year-end pricing bonus, expands Bilt partnership
items.description: United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM) this week announced the launch of a year-end pricing incentive for broker loans and an expansion of its partnership with Bilt . Effective immediately through Dec. 31, brokers who use UWM’s Underwriting+ , TRAC+ or virtual closing tools will receive 40 basis points on all agency and nonagency products when the borrower has a credit score of at least 700, UWM said. The incentive is intended to give brokers more pricing flexibility in the final weeks of 2026 while encouraging use of the lender’s underwriting and closing technology. Year-end pricing specials are common in the wholesale channel as lenders seek to pull volume into the current year, clean up pipelines and help partners hit production goals. UWM – which was more aggressive on pricing in the past but is seeking to deleverage its balance sheet amid a deal with Oaktree Capital Management and the Ishbia family – saw its gain-on-sale margins decline to 124 basis points in the third quarter, down from 133 basis points in the second quarter. UWM chairman, CEO and president Mat Ishbia told analysts he expects margins to be steady, adding that “people don’t use UWM because we’re the lowest rates” and arguing that competitors offering lower rates are not good partners. Separately, UWM said it's expanding its partnership with Bilt, a neighborhood commerce and rewards platform, to bring Bilt Neighborhood OS into its servicing ecosystem. Bilt Neighborhood OS is designed to help businesses reach customers and build loyalty through neighborhood-level experiences. Through UWM, it links mortgage servicing with homeownership tasks and local commerce, while keeping independent brokers visible to borrowers after closing. “The broker who helps you buy your home should be your first call when you’re ready to take the next step, whether that’s refinancing, accessing equity or buying again,” Ishbia said in a statement. “With Bilt Neighborhood OS, we’re making the servicing experience more valuable to homeowners and creating more reasons for them to stay connected to their broker between those major decisions.” UWM already services hundreds of thousands of loans through Bilt, giving these homeowners a single place to manage their mortgage and access rewards. With Neighborhood OS added, UWM said the experience will extend into more day-to-day homeownership activities, from finding a local contractor to exploring neighborhood offers, or reconnecting with a broker about a home equity or refinance opportunity. Bilt said it has delivered more than $1 billion in value to its 8 million members, who redeem rewards toward travel, housing payments, student loans , dining and other categories. The company also says it powers one in four U.S. rental homes , primarily through the Bilt Alliance of large owners and operators. items.title: 5 Pension Funds Join Shareholder Revolt Threatening H&R REIT Breakup Plan
items.description: A growing chorus of shareholders is revolting against the proposed $4.7B breakup of H&R REIT ahead of a vote on the deal Friday. Unsplash/Element5 Digital Five institutional shareholders have disclosed plans to vote against the transaction, according to proxy voting records reviewed by Bloomberg , and at least four other shareholders have said they plan to vote against the deal. The group is opposing the deal, which came after a review of strategic alternatives, in part because the buyout price has been chipped away. The deal to sell off the REIT's assets was struck in August and promised investors in Toronto-based H&R 4.28 Canadian dollars in cash plus 0.57 shares in GO Residential REIT for each of their H&R shares. At the time, the cash-and-stock deal was worth CA$12.01 per share and gave the REIT a total enterprise value of CA$6.7B, or roughly $4.7B. But shares in GO Residential have been sliding since the deal was announced, whittling away the value for investors to roughly CA$10.13 per share, according to Bloomberg. The New York City comptroller, California State Teachers’ Retirement System , State Board of Administration of Florida, British Columbia Investment Management Corp. and Norwegian pension fund KLP all plan to vote against the deal. RBC Global Asset Management, which holds 9.3 million units in H&R, and Mill Pond Capital, which has 2.2 million units, previously came out against the deal in October and were joined by Scheer Rowlett & Associates and Sandpiper Asset Management. The four investors control a combined 19 million units, or roughly 7% of H&R outstanding units, Bloomberg estimates. The size of the stakes of the five pension funds that oppose the deal isn’t public. Two shareholder advisory firms, Institutional Shareholder Services Inc. and Glass Lewis & Co., also advised H&R investors to vote against the breakup, Bloomberg reported. H&R must secure approval from two-thirds of votes cast across two voting tests and a majority in a third vote of unaffiliated unitholders to win approval for the deal, which would break up the REIT's assets between Blackstone Real Estate , Crestpoint Real Estate Investments , PSP Investments and a company controlled by the family of H&R CEO Tom Hofstedter. The deal, first rumored to be in negotiations in June, would send 27 properties to GO Residential, which launched last year to invest in luxury high-rise multifamily assets. Blackstone , PSP and Crestpoint would acquire H&R’s Canadian industrial properties in the deal, and the Hofstedter family would absorb H&R’s remaining noncore assets. H&R estimated the fair market value of its portfolio at $6.5B at the end of the second quarter. The REIT had been shedding assets, including $1.5B of retail and office property sales in the first quarter, for several years as part of a strategic rotation into the multifamily and industrial sectors. items.title: Skydance Eyes Real Estate Cuts, Consolidation In $6B Cost-Saving Push
items.description: James Gunn’s exit might not be the only shake-up happening at Skydance . Google Maps 1515 Broadway in New York, home to Skydance headquarters The David Ellison -led media empire Skydance, formed from the merger of Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount , is eyeing real estate cuts as it looks to move employees out of rented offices and into company-owned properties in Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta and London, CoStar News reported . The potential moves are part of an effort to save billions of dollars in annual spending. Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz said on a Monday earnings call that the company hopes to achieve at least $2.2B in savings by reducing real estate and facility overhead at Warner Bros. and Paramount. “There's also a very meaningful opportunity to rationalize our office footprint,” Kreiz said. “This includes consolidating our real estate across major markets." He said Skydance has five sites in New York, seven in Los Angeles, and multiple sites in Atlanta and London. Skydance, which completed its $111B merger last month, controls about 13M SF across 120 properties on top of “millions of square feet” leased from third-party landlords, according to CoStar. In New York, Paramount has a lease for 1.6M SF at One Astor Place at 1515 Broadway through 2031 and has another 185K SF at 555 W. 57th St. through 2029. Paramount also has 797K SF in Columbia Square in Los Angeles' Hollywood through 2028 and offices in Santa Monica , California, through 2034, CoStar reported. Third-party landlords with exposure to Skydance units include Kilroy Realty , Worthe Real Estate Group and Stockbridge , CoStar found. Earlier this week, Skydance announced that it was replacing DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran with former Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham, The Hollywood Reporter reported . Ellison also outlined other cost-cutting measures, including bundling HBO Max and Paramount+ streaming services together next year, in an effort to eliminate $6B in expenses in three years as it wrangles with $80B in debt. Skydance in its merged form spent about $8B in corporate overhead, including real estate, this year, according to the LA Times . items.description: Veterans own homes at much higher rates than non-veterans, a gap driven in part by access to specialized mortgage programs that are also helping narrow racial homeownership disparities, according to an analysis of 2024 American Community Survey data for the nation’s 50 largest metro areas. The veteran homeownership rate was 77% in 2024, compared to 60% for non-veterans. Among adults under 35, 46.6% of veterans were homeowners versus 31.9% of non-veterans, showing that military service is associated with earlier entry into homeownership. Homeownership remains the primary path to wealth for U.S. households. Federal Reserve data show the median wealth of a typical homeowner is more than 40 times the median wealth of a typical renter, underscoring why access to mortgage credit and affordable payments is central to closing wealth gaps. Veteran advantage strongest in Virginia Beach, Memphis and Fresno Among the 50 largest metro areas, Virginia Beach, Virginia, has both the highest concentration of veterans and the largest homeownership advantage for that population. In Virginia Beach, 80% of veterans own homes, compared with 57.4% of non-veterans. Other large metros where veterans significantly outperform civilians on homeownership include: Memphis, Tennessee: 80.2% veteran homeownership vs. 58.4% for non-veterans Fresno, California: 76.6% vs. 54.7% New York, New York: 73.9% vs. 53.7% San Diego, California: 71.7% vs. 51.8% Veterans also see a notable edge in high-cost coastal markets where civilian homeownership is constrained by high prices. In places like New York, San Diego and Fresno, access to 0% down payment financing through the VA loan program can provide a substantial relative boost for eligible buyers compared to civilians reliant on conventional financing. Young veterans see outsized gains The homeownership advantage is particularly pronounced for veterans under 35. In Memphis, 66% of young veterans are homeowners, compared with 46.9% of young non-veterans, a 19.1 percentage point gap. Other top metros for young veteran homeownership include: Fresno, California: 65.5% young veteran homeownership vs. 47.3% for young non-veterans, an 18.2 percentage point advantage Virginia Beach, Virginia: 63.4% vs. 47.1%, a 16.3 percentage point advantage Buffalo, New York: 71.9% vs. 58.4%, a 13.5 percentage point advantage Providence, Rhode Island: 67% vs. 54.2%, a 12.8 percentage point advantage While younger veterans still have lower homeownership rates than older veterans, they are substantially more likely to own homes than their non-veteran peers. For lenders and real estate agents, that indicates a distinct demand segment for first-time buyer products and education tailored to veteran households. Military service linked to smaller racial homeownership gaps The analysis also finds that veteran status is associated with reduced racial disparities in homeownership. Across the 50 largest metros, overall homeownership rates are 72.1% for white households and 49.5% for non-white households, reflecting a long history of segregation and discrimination in housing. Among veteran households, however, the white-nonwhite homeownership gap shrinks to 13.6 percentage points, as military service appears to elevate non-white homeownership rates. Several large metros show particularly small racial gaps among veterans: Riverside–San Bernardino, California: 82.1% homeownership for white veterans vs. 75% for non-white veterans, a 7.1 percentage point gap Tampa–St. Petersburg, Florida: 83.1% vs. 75.5%, a 7.6 percentage point gap San Antonio, Texas: 82.6% vs. 74.9%, a 7.7 percentage point gap Las Vegas, Nevada: 74.3% vs. 66.6%, a 7.7 percentage point gap Fresno, California: 78.3% vs. 69.6%, an 8.7 percentage point gap For policymakers and housing practitioners focused on equity, these patterns suggest that veteran-specific benefits and underwriting frameworks may offer lessons for reducing racial gaps in the broader market. In fiscal year 2025, the VA guaranteed 323,835 purchase loans, according to the analysis. VA purchase loans allow eligible veterans and service members to buy with zero down payment and no ongoing monthly mortgage insurance. Because the loans are backed by a partial federal guarantee, they typically feature lower interest rates, capped closing costs and more flexible qualification standards than conventional loans. items.title: MLS roundup: AI, fraud prevention and data sharing take center stage
items.description: MLS organizations are expanding their technology offerings with new partnerships focused on artificial intelligence, property fraud prevention and access to listing data. The latest developments include tools designed to streamline agents' work, protect listing information and improve property research across markets. Big Sky Country MLS adds fraud protection for 1,600 subscribers Big Sky Country MLS in Montana has partnered with Property Shield to provide fraud detection and prevention services to all 1,600 subscribers. Beginning in November, agents will receive protection against fraudulent listings, along with support for removing unauthorized property advertisements. The MLS will also use Property Shield's automated IDX compliance monitoring to identify potential violations across licensed data feeds. The partnership addresses the growing problem of scammers copying legitimate listings to solicit deposits from unsuspecting buyers and renters. Flexmls launches Scout AI assistant for MLS subscribers FBS has introduced Flexmls Scout, an AI assistant that allows real estate professionals to search MLS data, analyze market activity and access business insights using natural-language questions. Built directly into Flexmls, Scout uses permissioned MLS information and enterprise controls to help agents research properties and understand market trends without switching platforms. The product is available to Flexmls MLS customers as an enterprise solution. Stellar MLS and MIBOR expand property data sharing across state lines Stellar MLS in Florida and MIBOR Broker Listing Cooperative in Indiana have announced a data-sharing agreement through Realtors Property Resource's RPR View platform. The collaboration gives eligible subscribers access to approved off-market listings and historical property data across both MLS markets . The agreement is designed to help agents serving relocating homeowners, seasonal residents and buyers with real estate interests in both states. LERA MLS brings RealReports AI platform to 15,000 agents LERA MLS has partnered with RealReports to provide more than 15,000 subscribers across San Antonio and South Texas access to its AI-powered property intelligence platform. RealReports combines property research, prospecting, comparative market analysis and client engagement tools with information covering more than 150 million U.S. properties. Its AI assistant, Aiden, helps agents identify potential business opportunities and provide clients with more detailed property insights. California Realtors gain access to property fraud-prevention platform EquityProtect has partnered with Real Estate Business Services, the for-profit subsidiary of the California Association of Realtors , to make its property fraud-prevention platform available to association members. The program provides tools to help agents educate homeowners about deed theft, seller impersonation and other property fraud risks. The partnership is designed to help agents maintain relationships with clients beyond closing while offering preventive protection. HAR.com and LERA MLS partner to bring platinum technology platform to San Antonio Realtors HAR.com and LERA Multiple Listing Service have announced a new partnership that will give LERA MLS subscribers the opportunity to subscribe to HAR.com’s Platinum technology platform. Platinum is HAR.com's subscription-based suite of marketing and productivity tools designed to help real estate professionals grow their business, strengthen their brand and work more efficiently. It was developed by HAR.com’s in-house technology team in 2016 and includes tools for lead generation, client relationship management, marketing and market insights. The partnership with LERA MLS marks the first expansion of HAR.com's Platinum platform outside the Greater Houston area. Since its launch, Platinum has grown from 11 tools to nearly 60 and is now used by more than 20,000 HAR MLS subscribers. The buyer, Centennial Holding Co. LLC, purchased the property from an undisclosed seller. Cliff Taylor, Joe Ayers, Kyle Butler and Ted Taylor of JLL represented the seller and procured the buyer in the transaction. Additionally, Melissa Quinn and Matt Kafka, also with JLL, originated a seven-year Freddie Mac acquisition loan for Centennial Holding. The sales price and loan amount were not disclosed. Built in 2024, The Juliette sits on 21.8 acres near The Villages master-planned community in Central Florida and was 96 percent occupied at the time of sale. The property comprises 288 apartments and 42 townhomes averaging 971 square feet in size. items.description: Why Michael Lynd sees a ‘misalignment’ between apartment sponsor and investment interest The CEO of Kairoi Residential thinks some multifamily owners may be making a mistake by “opting to kick the can down the road” in hopes the rental environment will suddenly improve. Published Nov. 11, 2026 Leslie Shaver Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Waterline in Austin, Texas. Permission granted by Kairoi Residential Listen to the article 8 min This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback . A number of property management groups across the country are aggressively growing by scooping up smaller operators to expand into new markets. Michael Lynd, the CEO of Kairoi Residential, said he’s also looking to expand, but he’s being more selective. “We don't just want to be everywhere,” Lynd said. “We'll turn down assignments if it's a non-core market for us. We don't have an ambition to be in every market in the United States.” Still, San Antonio-based Kairoi, which ranked No. 45 on the most recent National Multifamily Housing Council Top 50 Managers list, is “moving toward a national presence” in apartment management as it works to meet the needs of an evolving client base. “The reasoning behind that is that our clients continue to show an interest in working with less management companies, not more,” Lynd said. “So they're consolidating their businesses and their management assignments among fewer and fewer managers, which allows their asset managers to be more efficient.” Kairoi’s management business “is very selective and operates in the high-end niche, specifically,” Lynd said. Third-party management accounts for 75% of that business, which focuses primarily on institutional clients and core and core-plus properties, he said. With that focus, Kairoi isn’t pursuing the same merger-and-acquisition opportunities as its peers. “If it's just a roll-up game that you're hoping to play without an outcome, I think that's a different business model than what we're living under,” Lynd said. “Our business model is different. We’re going to be Formula 1 drivers. There are only a few of them, and they're really, really, really good at what they do.” Management isn’t Kairoi’s only line of business. The firm invests in existing apartments and co-developed Waterline, a 74-story mixed-use tower in Austin, Texas, with Lincoln Property Co. The tower includes Bosque Residences, a 352-unit apartment community. Kairoi has also built condos, for-sale homes and other large mixed-use projects, according to Lynd. Lynd took some time to speak with Multifamily Dive about his company’s ventures and broader industry topics, including how he analyzes new markets, the roadblocks to development and the mistakes many struggling owners are making right now. This interview has been edited for brevity and clarity. MULTIFAMILY DIVE: How do you gear up to move into new markets? MICHAEL LYND: We want to do it strategically in markets where we can compete and where we feel like we've got great talent. We're always hiring the talent ahead of that growth and subsidizing those markets until they get up and running. Our goal is to have 8,000 to 10,000 units per market. That's what we have in our mature markets generally. We will usually start with an existing client in a lot of these markets where we don't have a presence. But we have entered a lot of markets extremely successfully. We manage some amazing assets across the board, whether that be in Salt Lake or Charlotte. Those are more of newer markets that are starting to mature in terms of their unit counts. We're getting more and more assets and more and more at-bats and more and more pitches in those markets now regularly. And then there are new markets like Nashville and Atlanta, South Florida and Southern California. What other areas are you interested in? We continue to broaden our geographic footprint. I could see us going up to the mid-Atlantic, all the way down to Florida, up and down the West Coast and throughout the South. We want to be in markets where we will either invest in and/or develop in. Not all markets will be developed in because we don't think every market provides us the same leverage for our balance sheet. So we're very protective about where we are spending that balance sheet capital from a development perspective. We will continue to grow. It's been an extremely busy month [in October] for us on the property management side of our business. Development has been a challenge and continues to be, with interest rates and construction costs. Is access to equity the main development roadblock that you’re facing? It's a lack of equity, and it's really a lack of clarity about where these markets are headed. We've made a lot of investments in technology and data, and in mining our own data. And then mapping and graphing and categorizing that data so that we aren't just making decisions off of CoStar and other data services, which we also subscribe to. But there's nothing better than our own data. So we're using that to make decisions and assess market conditions. The good news is we're seeing the best submarkets in most, if not all, of our markets really generating positive rent trade-outs now. So that's great to see. It's broader in places like Austin, Dallas, and then a smaller geographic representation in a place like Denver. We’re seeing positive momentum. items.title: Inside UT Dallas’ 24-Hour Hackathon
items.description: Live Poll Over 1,200 collegiate tech savants from around the world filled the engineering and computer science buildings of UTD’s campus for HackUTD, North America’s largest 24-hour university hackathon . The vision: inspire students to innovate and learn new technologies. HackUTD is propelling creativity in tech by cultivating a day where curious minds puzzle to build software and hardware prototypes guided by prompts that will stretch their knowledge and skills. Hailey Muniz, a 20-year-old sophomore from UTSA and Camille Rivera, a 21-year-old senior from UTSA, shared their excitement about coming to HackUTD. “I’ve been dreaming of coming here since I was a freshman. The opportunities to build and meet new people are really great”, says Muniz. “These high-pressure situations allow for the most amount of creativity and the most amount of networking," says Rivera. "Seeing everyone around me working so hard and towards something they’re proud of really inspires me to keep going." Around 10 a.m., UTD’s auditorium was overflowing with students listening to prompt challenging them to create technical solutions that will require teamwork and a whole lot of caffeine. By 12 p.m., students raced off to settle into groups where they would work through the night using everything they’ve learned and technologies they aren’t as familiar with. Companies like State Farm and T-Mobile had help desks set up to provide guidance and troubleshooting from their own engineers in unfamiliar areas. I asked Nikita Kelwada, a 21-year-old senior from Texas A&M, how she planned to leverage AI in her development time. “I want to restrict myself from using it too much. I don’t want to vibe code my entire project; I want to learn the technologies," Kelwada says. "I’ll probably do some research on what technologies would be useful and then use AI to help me figure out what specific pathways or what specific databases to use.” One theme ran throughout each student’s ambition: To build technology that would help people. “I’m planning to build a hardware project that’s specifically aimed towards impacting people and improving their quality of life,” says Rivera. Vedha Vaddepally, a 20-year-old UTD junior, shared that he wants to develop his own AI model in the future designed to help others. For those outside the computer science community, our future with AI feels uncertain. But for those who understand the inner workings of machine learning technologies, the future looks bright. items.title: Houston single-family home sales dip 15% in October
items.description: Houston single-family home sales dip 15% in October by Emily Marek November 11, 2026 Home sales declined 14.9% year over year in Houston, with 6,348 closings during October. (via HAR) Options increased for Houston homebuyers in October as the market pace slowed, according to the latest Housing Market Update from the Houston Association of REALTORS® . Home sales declined 14.9% year over year, with 6,348 closings during the month. Despite the steep decline in home sales in October, year-to-date sales lagged behind 2025 volumes by just 2%. The average home price was steady at $421,100, while the median dipped 3% to $320,000 — the lowest price since January 2024, HAR said. Meanwhile, active listings remained high, with 40,253 properties on the market. That was up 6.8% from a year prior. Given the rate of sales, that gave the Houston area a 5.5-month inventory, unchanged from September but matching the highest level since 2012. “Consumers are paying close attention to the economy and their household budgets, so it is understandable that some buyers are taking more time before purchasing a home,” said HAR Chair Theresa Hill. “We typically see activity ease as the year winds down, but buyers who are still looking may have more time to find a home that fits their needs and budget.” Affordability decreased annually: Given the average mortgage rate of 7.33%, October buyers had a monthly mortgage payment of $1,760.28 — $134.79 higher than a year ago. “Affordability remains a challenge for homebuyers, and the possibility of a quarter-point interest rate increase by the Federal Reserve before the end of the year could add further pressure to the housing market,” said HAR Chief Economist Ted Jones . Existing-home sales Among only existing single-family homes (excluding new construction ), closings fell 10.2%. The average price decreased marginally to $428,790, and the median fell 4.5% to $315,000. Townhome and condominium sales Looking at for-sale townhomes and condos, sales plummeted 23.5% year over year with 336 closings during the month. The average price increased 5.6% to $263,413, while the median fell 3.7% to $197,500. Given the rate of sales, Houston’s townhome/condo inventory was a whopping 9.4 months, up from 8.2 months a year prior. items.title: Hurricane Season Is Over Early, but El Niño Is Not Done With Us Yet
items.description: In a typical year, the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June to the end of November. But 2026 has been anything but a typical year. In fact, the meteorologists at AccuWeather have announced that tropical activity for the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season is over, three weeks before the official end of the season on Nov. 30. The reason? "El Niño has played a significant role in limiting tropical activity across the Atlantic," said AccuWeather lead hurricane expert Alex DaSilva . "While tropical storms can still develop this late in the season, the weather patterns we're seeing give us confidence that the United States will avoid additional direct tropical impacts this year. It's an unusually quiet conclusion to a season that defied expectations and broke a 121-year-old hurricane record.” But while the hurricane season might be bowing out early, the country still needs to prepare itself for the coming winter months in a big way. A quiet season AccuWeather originally forecasted 11 to 16 named storms for the season last spring, but once El Niño arrived and strengthened much earlier in the year than usual, the forecast dropped to eight to 11 named storms and three to four hurricanes. To date, only 10 named storms came to fruition, the fewest since 2014, when there were only eight storms. Only one reached hurricane status, with Hurricane Isaias making a destructive Category 2 landfall on the Florida Panhandle in October. It was the first time since 1925 that there was only one hurricane in the entire season. That’s not to say that the season wasn’t destructive. The first storm of the season, Tropical Storm Arthur , dumped more than 20 inches of rain in some spots across the Gulf in June and caused an estimated $4 billion to $6 billion in total damage and economic loss, according to a preliminary estimate from experts at AccuWeather . Loading... Loading... Hurricanes out, but wet weather remains While the hurricane season is over, homeowners across the country still have to continue with a deluge of wet weather on the way. Again, all thanks to the Super El Niño still churning away. Notably, the El Niño could influence winter weather across the United States, bringing warmer-than-average temperatures to Northern states and wetter-than-average conditions to the South and East Coast, according to NOAA’s U.S. Winter Outlook . Wetter-than-average conditions are most likely across the southern tier, from the Southwest to the Southeast, and along the East Coast. But if the temperatures stay up, the likelihood of snow is slim. But even without the snow , the storms could be significant for this area this year. “As we know from decades of observations, a very strong El Nino will likely bring a southward and eastward shift to the jet stream for the contiguous U.S., which tilts the odds toward stormier weather across the South,” said Ken Graham , director of NOAA’s National Weather Service. “While higher chances of rain and snow may bring relief to drought-afflicted areas, too much precipitation on dry soil can fuel destructive flash floods and mudslides. Now is the time for communities and individuals to plan ahead for the upcoming winter.” Meanwhile, more snow than average is favored across parts of the Intermountain West, the Plains, and the Appalachians this winter because of El Niño's active storm track, according to The Wall Street Journal . In fact, most models that were reviewed showed above-average snowfall across the Plains, from South Dakota to northern Texas , and a swath of the central and southern Appalachians. Dina Sartore-Bodo is the senior editor at Realtor.com covering real estate news, personal finance trends, and interior design. She previously served as the managing editor at HollywoodLife.com, the executive editor at PerezHilton.com, and as a managing editor at Mediavine. Her work has also appeared on MSN, Yahoo News, and BlogHer. She is a proud graduate of Emerson College in Boston and is originally from New Jersey.

Lambert argued in the 12-page complaint that the problems in his unit were caused by repairs to the building’s facade that had been performed by a contractor, for which he paid over $15,000 as part of a special assessment. items.title: Home Sales Plunge to 16-Year Low as High Mortgage Rates Derail Deals
items.description: Existing-home sales suffered a historic setback in October, as surging mortgage rates made shoppers hit the pause button on their homebuying plans. According to the latest data from the National Association of Realtors® released on Thursday, existing-home sales plunged to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, down 5.5% from September 's downwardly revised pace of 3.97 million, and 8.8% from a year ago. This marks the lowest market pace since August 2010, during the aftermath of the Great Recession. "Homebuying is difficult when mortgage rates have climbed to their highest levels since 2000, aside from a single month in 2023," says NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun . Notably, sales fell annually across every price tier in October, even in the $1 million-and-up market that had previously proven resilient. The median sales price reached $416,700 last month, inching up just 0.4% from a year ago, the highest for the month of October. Meanwhile, inventory expanded by 1.3% month over month and 4.6% year over year to 1.59 million housing units, a seven-year high. This translates into 5.1 months' supply, which is the highest level in 11 years. Loading... "Despite fewer transactions in October, the 88 million homeowners across the country are largely in a comfortable financial position due to sizable housing wealth accumulation," notes Yun. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage in September averaged 7.33% in October, up from 6.86% in September, according to Freddie Mac. The rate hit a three-year high of 7.40% on Oct. 8 but has been gradually retreating over the past four weeks. "Higher mortgage rates certainly discouraged buyers looking for new homes," says Yun. "So right now, the market's overall condition is challenging buyers and sellers." Across the board decline Regionally, month-over-month sales declined by the widest margin in the West (-9.7%), followed by the South (-6.5%), and the Midwest (-3.2%), but held steady in the Northeast. Year-over-year sales slid in all four regions, with the West experiencing the sharpest pullback, at 14.5%. Realtor.com® Chief Economist Danielle Hale predicts that home sales are likely to remain relatively low for the rest of 2026 as mortgage rates remain high, yet she does not believe it is the new normal. "Instead, it reflects a perfect storm of an abrupt shift in the financial environment and large uncertainties in the pre-election period for both policy and the economy just as the housing market usually slows for the season," says Hale. "While they won’t last long-term, these challenges are likely to keep home sales near longtime lows for the next few months." October saw affordability fall across the U.S. The national housing affordability index registered at 100.7, down from 107.3 a year ago. At the same time, all four regions felt the squeeze, with the expensive, undersupplied Northeast shedding 8.7% off its affordability index, followed by the Midwest (-7.2%), the South (-5.4%), and the West (-5.2%). Reflecting the eroding affordability, the share of first-time homebuyers shrank from 31% in September to 29% in October. However, cash buying increased from 27% in September to 29% in October thanks to the record equity that homeowners have accumulated. On a positive note, the number of foreclosure sales remains historically low at 2% of all transactions. "Based on the current underwhelming home sales pace at a time of consistent job growth, there could be sizable pent-up demand if mortgage rates decline," says Yun. Looking ahead, Hale says she expects more homebuyers to come off the sidelines as the market moves away from recent mortgage rate highs, but with a major caveat. "Several factors are likely to put a floor under how low rates can go, including a strong economy and jobs market , persistent inflation , and an expected need for tighter monetary policy in the near term combined with sizable demand for capital from both governments and private companies, largely to finance AI-related investments," she says. Snejana Farberov is a reporter at Realtor.com covering the U.S. housing market and the latest domestic real estate trends. She has worked as a general assignment journalist in New York City and Long Island for 16 years, writing for New York Post, Daily Mail, and News 12. Snejana earned bachelor's degrees in journalism and Italian from St. John's University, followed by a master’s degree from Columbia University School of Journalism.
